1984
1985    @property
1986    def rows(self) -> Range:
1987        """``Range`` over data rows; ``height`` sets row heights.
1988
1989        ``table.rows[i]`` uses **data-row** indices: ``0`` is the first body
1990        row at the current origin (top by default, bottom when
1991        ``from_bottom_left`` is True). This differs from ``table.cells[i, …]``,
1992        which uses **grid-row** indices.
1993
1994        Examples:
1995            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
1996            >>> _ = table.add_row(1)
1997            >>> table.rows._size_axis
1998            'rows'
1999        """
2000        column_count, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
2001        if column_count == 0:
2002            return Range(self, 0, 0, -1, -1, size_axis="rows")
2003        public_rows = _public_body_grid_rows(self)
2004        if not public_rows:
2005            return Range(self, 0, 0, -1, -1, size_axis="rows")
2006        return Range(
2007            self,
2008            public_rows[0],
2009            0,
2010            public_rows[-1],
2011            column_count - 1,
2012            size_axis="rows",
2013            explicit_grid_rows=tuple(public_rows),
2014        )
2015
2016    @property
2017    def cells(self) -> Range:
2018        """``Range`` over the full grid (header row included when present).
2019
2020        Index as ``table.cells[grid_row, col]`` — both axes 0-based **grid**
2021        indices. Row numbering follows the table origin. With explicit headers
2022        and ``show_header=True``, the header is row ``0`` only when
2023        ``from_bottom_left`` is False; with ``from_bottom_left=True`` the header
2024        is the last grid row. For body-only row numbers use :meth:`cell` or
2025        :meth:`populate` instead.
2026
2027        Examples:
2028            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2029            >>> _ = table.add_row("z")
2030            >>> table.cells[0, 0].content
2031            'A'
2032            >>> table.cells[1, 0].content
2033            'z'
2034            >>> table.cell(1, 0).content
2035            'z'
2036        """
2037        column_count, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
2038        if column_count == 0 or grid_row_count == 0:
2039            return _empty_grid_range(self)
2040        public_rows = tuple(_public_full_grid_rows(self))
2041        return Range(
2042            self,
2043            0,
2044            0,
2045            grid_row_count - 1,
2046            column_count - 1,
2047            explicit_grid_rows=public_rows,
2048        )
2049
2050    def range(
2051        self,
2052        row_start: int,
2053        col_start: int,
2054        row_end: int,
2055        col_end: int,
2056    ) -> Range:
2057        """Return an inclusive rectangular region (0-based grid indices).
2058
2059        Same row/column convention as :attr:`cells`: grid row ``0`` is the
2060        first row at the current origin. The header is included only when
2061        explicit headers exist and ``show_header`` is True. Column indices start
2062        at ``0``.
2063
2064        Args:
2065            row_start: Top grid row of the range.
2066            col_start: Left column index.
2067            row_end: Bottom grid row of the range.
2068            col_end: Right column index.
2069
2070        Examples:
2071            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2072            >>> _ = table.add_row(1, 2)
2073            >>> table.range(1, 0, 1, 0).content
2074            1
2075        """
2076        public_rows = _public_full_grid_rows(self)
2077        start = min(row_start, row_end)
2078        end = max(row_start, row_end)
2079        picked_rows = public_rows[start : end + 1]
2080        return Range(
2081            self,
2082            picked_rows[0],
2083            col_start,
2084            picked_rows[-1],
2085            col_end,
2086            explicit_grid_rows=tuple(picked_rows),
2087        )
2088
2089    def _sizes_for_span(
2090        self,
2091        span: int,
2092        size: float | Sequence[float],
2093        *,
2094        kind: str,
2095    ) -> list[float]:
2096        if isinstance(size, Sequence) and not isinstance(size, (str, bytes)):
2097            values = list(size)
2098            if len(values) != span:
2099                raise ValueError(
2100                    f"{kind} size sequence length {len(values)} "
2101                    f"does not match range span {span}"
2102                )
2103            return values
2104        return [float(size)] * span
2105
2106    def _apply_column_widths(
2107        self,
2108        col_start: int,
2109        col_end: int,
2110        size: float | Sequence[float],
2111    ) -> None:
2112        span = col_end - col_start + 1
2113        if span <= 0:
2114            raise ValueError("width assignment on an empty range")
2115        for col_index, width in zip(
2116            range(col_start, col_end + 1),
2117            self._sizes_for_span(span, size, kind="column"),
2118            strict=True,
2119        ):
2120            self._columns[col_index]._width = width
2121        self._invalidate_layout()
2122
2123    def _apply_grid_row_heights(
2124        self,
2125        row_start: int,
2126        row_end: int,
2127        size: float | Sequence[float],
2128    ) -> None:
2129        span = row_end - row_start + 1
2130        if span <= 0:
2131            raise ValueError("height assignment on an empty range")
2132        for grid_row, height in zip(
2133            range(row_start, row_end + 1),
2134            self._sizes_for_span(span, size, kind="row"),
2135            strict=True,
2136        ):
2137            if _has_header_row(self) and grid_row == 0:
2138                self._header_row_height = height
2139            else:
2140                data_row = grid_row - (1 if _has_header_row(self) else 0)
2141                self._rows[data_row]._height = height
2142        self._invalidate_layout()
2143
2144    def _cell_at_grid(self, grid_row: int, col_index: int) -> Cell:
2145        column_count, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
2146        if col_index < 0 or col_index >= column_count:
2147            raise IndexError(f"column index {col_index} out of range")
2148        if grid_row < 0 or grid_row >= grid_row_count:
2149            raise IndexError(f"grid row {grid_row} out of range")
2150        if _has_header_row(self) and grid_row == 0:
2151            return self._columns[col_index].header_cell
2152        data_row = grid_row - (1 if _has_header_row(self) else 0)
2153        return self._rows[data_row].cells[col_index]
2154
2155    def cell(self, row_index: int, col_index: int) -> Cell:
2156        """Return the cell at ``(row_index, col_index)``.
2157
2158        Row ``0`` is the header when a header row is shown. The next row is
2159        ``1``. With no header, row ``0`` is the first body row.
2160        ``col_index`` ``0`` is the leftmost column.
2161
2162        Examples:
2163            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2164            >>> _ = table.add_row("v")
2165            >>> table.cell(0, 0).content
2166            'A'
2167            >>> table.cell(1, 0).content
2168            'v'
2169        """
2170        if _has_header_row(self):
2171            return self._cell_at_grid(row_index, col_index)
2172        storage_index = _storage_row_index(self, row_index)
2173        return self._rows[storage_index].cells[col_index]
2174
2175    def column(self, col_index: int) -> Column:
2176        """Return the column at ``col_index``.
2177
2178        Examples:
2179            >>> table = Table(columns=["H"])
2180            >>> table.column(0).header
2181            'H'
2182        """
2183        return self._columns[col_index]
2184
2185    def row(self, row_index: int) -> Row:
2186        """Return the data row at ``row_index`` (0-based, header excluded).
2187
2188        Examples:
2189            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2190            >>> _ = table.add_row(9)
2191            >>> table.row(0).cells[0].content
2192            9
2193        """
2194        storage_index = _storage_row_index(self, row_index)
2195        return self._rows[storage_index]
2196
2197    def set_format(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Self:
2198        """Apply format to the table and every cell (including headers).
2199
2200        Examples:
2201            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2202            >>> _ = table.set_format(font_size=14)
2203            >>> table.font_size
2204            14
2205        """
2206        self._format.update(kwargs)
2207        if "font_size" in kwargs:
2208            object.__setattr__(self, "font_size", kwargs["font_size"])
2209        for column in self._columns:
2210            column.set_format(**kwargs)
2211        for row in self._rows:
2212            row.set_format(**kwargs)
2213        self._invalidate_layout()
2214        return self
2215
2216    def set_background(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Self:
2217        """Apply background to the table and every cell (including headers).
2218
2219        Examples:
2220            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2221            >>> _ = table.set_background(fill=True)
2222            >>> table._background["fill"]
2223            True
2224        """
2225        self._background.update(kwargs)
2226        for column in self._columns:
2227            column.set_background(**kwargs)
2228        for row in self._rows:
2229            row.set_background(**kwargs)
2230        return self
2231
2232    def reset(self) -> Self:
2233        """Empty all cells and clear table, row, column, and cell styling.
2234
2235        The table keeps its current row and column counts, title, position,
2236        and visibility settings. Header labels are cleared because header cells
2237        are part of the grid.
2238
2239        Examples:
2240            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2241            >>> table = sg.Table(columns=["A"], size=(1, 1))
2242            >>> table.cell(0, 0).content = "x"
2243            >>> _ = table.column(0).set_format(align=sg.Align.RIGHT)
2244            >>> table.rows.height = 24
2245            >>> table.reset() is table
2246            True
2247            >>> table.column_headers
2248            ['']
2249            >>> table.cell(0, 0).content
2250            ''
2251            >>> table.column(0)._format
2252            {}
2253            >>> table.row(0)._height is None
2254            True
2255        """
2256        self.font_size = _TABLE_DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE
2257        self._format = {}
2258        self._background = {}
2259        self._header_row_height = self._default_row_height
2260
2261        for column in self._columns:
2262            column._format = {}
2263            column._background = {}
2264            column._width = self._default_column_width
2265            column.header = ""
2266            column.header_cell._format = {}
2267            column.header_cell._background = {}
2268
2269        for row in self._rows:
2270            row._format = {}
2271            row._background = {}
2272            row._height = self._default_row_height
2273            for cell in row.cells:
2274                cell.content = ""
2275                cell._format = {}
2276                cell._background = {}
2277
2278        self._invalidate_layout()
2279        return self
2280
2281    def _invalidate_layout(self) -> None:
2282        object.__setattr__(self, "_layout_revision", self._layout_revision + 1)
2283        object.__setattr__(self, "_layout_cache_key", None)
2284        object.__setattr__(self, "_layout_cache", None)
2285
2286    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
2287        target = _range_style_target(name)
2288        if target is None:
2289            raise AttributeError(
2290                f"'{type(self).__name__}' object has no attribute '{name}'"
2291            )
2292        kind, storage_name = target
2293        store = self._format if kind == "format" else self._background
2294        if storage_name not in store:
2295            return None
2296        return store[storage_name]
2297
2298    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: Any) -> None:
2299        if name.startswith("_"):
2300            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
2301            return
2302        if "_format" not in vars(self):
2303            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
2304            return
2305        target = _range_style_target(name)
2306        if target is None:
2307            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
2308            if name in {"min_width", "padding", "show_header"}:
2309                self._invalidate_layout()
2310            return
2311        kind, storage_name = target
2312        if storage_name in ("align", "v_align"):
2313            value = _resolve_align(value)
2314        if kind == "format":
2315            self.set_format(**{storage_name: value})
2316            return
2317        self.set_background(**{storage_name: value})
2318
2319    @property
2320    def b_box(self) -> BoundingBox:
2321        """Axis-aligned box enclosing the grid and optional title.
2322
2323        Examples:
2324            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2325            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
2326            >>> table.b_box.width > 0
2327            True
2328        """
2329        boxes = [table_grid_bbox(self)]
2330        title_box = table_title_bbox(self)
2331        if title_box is not None:
2332            boxes.append(title_box)
2333        return _union_bounding_boxes(boxes)
2334
2335    def _column_bbox(self, col_index: int) -> BoundingBox:
2336        _, row_heights, column_count = compute_table_layout(self)
2337        if col_index >= column_count:
2338            return BoundingBox()
2339        boxes = [
2340            table_cell_bbox(self, grid_row, col_index)
2341            for grid_row in range(len(row_heights))
2342        ]
2343        return _union_bounding_boxes(boxes)
2344
2345    def _row_bbox(self, row_index: int) -> BoundingBox:
2346        _, row_heights, column_count = compute_table_layout(self)
2347        grid_row = _grid_row_from_data_row(self, row_index)
2348        if grid_row >= len(row_heights):
2349            return BoundingBox()
2350        boxes = [
2351            table_cell_bbox(self, grid_row, col_index)
2352            for col_index in range(column_count)
2353        ]
2354        return _union_bounding_boxes(boxes)
2355
2356    @property
2357    def corners(self) -> list[PointType]:
2358        """Bounding quadrilateral of the full table (northwest first).
2359
2360        Examples:
2361            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2362            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
2363            >>> len(table.corners)
2364            4
2365        """
2366        box = self.b_box
2367        if box.southwest is None:
2368            x, y = self.pos[:2]
2369            return [(x, y), (x, y), (x, y), (x, y)]
2370        return [
2371            box.northwest,
2372            box.northeast,
2373            box.southeast,
2374            box.southwest,
2375        ]
2376
2377    @property
2378    def all_vertices(self) -> list[PointType]:
2379        """Flattened corner vertices for bounding-box updates.
2380
2381        Examples:
2382            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2383            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
2384            >>> len(table.all_vertices) >= 4
2385            True
2386        """
2387        box = self.b_box
2388        if box.southwest is None:
2389            x, y = self.pos[:2]
2390            return [(x, y)]
2391        return list(box.corners)
2392
2393    def _append_column(self, header: str) -> Column:
2394        column = Column(self, len(self._columns), header)
2395        column._width = self._default_column_width
2396        self._columns.append(column)
2397        for row in self._rows:
2398            while len(row.cells) < len(self._columns):
2399                row.cells.append(Cell(""))
2400        self._invalidate_layout()
2401        return column
2402
2403    def add_column(
2404        self,
2405        header: str,
2406        align: Align | str = _TABLE_DEFAULT_COLUMN_ALIGN,
2407    ) -> Column:
2408        """Append a column and return its ``Column`` object.
2409
2410        Examples:
2411            >>> table = Table()
2412            >>> col = table.add_column("New")
2413            >>> col.header
2414            'New'
2415        """
2416        self._explicit_headers = True
2417        column = self._append_column(header)
2418        column.set_format(align=align)
2419        return column
2420
2421    def add_row(self, *cells: Any) -> Row:
2422        """Append one data row and return its ``Row`` object.
2423
2424        Examples:
2425            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2426            >>> row = table.add_row(1, 2)
2427            >>> row.cells[1].content
2428            2
2429        """
2430        if self._columns and len(cells) != len(self._columns):
2431            raise ValueError(
2432                f"Row has {len(cells)} cells but table has "
2433                f"{len(self._columns)} columns."
2434            )
2435        if not self._columns and cells:
2436            for _ in cells:
2437                self._append_column("")
2438        row = Row(self, len(self._rows), cells)
2439        row._height = self._default_row_height
2440        while len(row.cells) < len(self._columns):
2441            row.cells.append(Cell(""))
2442        if self.from_bottom_left:
2443            self._rows.insert(0, row)
2444        else:
2445            self._rows.append(row)
2446        for index, current_row in enumerate(self._rows):
2447            current_row.index = index
2448        self._invalidate_layout()
2449        return row
2450
2451    def _ensure_grid_covers(
2452        self,
2453        min_grid_row: int,
2454        max_grid_row: int,
2455        max_grid_col: int,
2456    ) -> None:
2457        if min_grid_row < 0 or max_grid_col < 0:
2458            raise IndexError("grid row or column index out of range")
2459        while len(self._columns) <= max_grid_col:
2460            self._append_column("")
2461        _, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
2462        while grid_row_count <= max_grid_row:
2463            self.add_row(*([""] * len(self._columns)))
2464            _, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
2465
2466    def populate(
2467        self,
2468        row: int,
2469        column: int,
2470        columns: int,
2471        items: Sequence[Any],
2472        from_bottom_left: bool = False,
2473    ) -> Self:
2474        """Fill a rectangle of body cells starting at ``(row, column)``.
2475
2476        All indices are 0-based. ``row`` and ``column`` are **data-row**
2477        indices (the header is not part of ``row``). :meth:`cell` counts the
2478        header as row ``0`` when a header is shown.
2479        Items are placed in row-major order with ``columns`` cells per row—the
2480        same layout as :func:`~simetri.helpers.utilities.get_cell_pos`. When
2481        ``from_bottom_left`` is False, filling continues at ``row + 1``,
2482        ``row + 2``, … in increasing data-row order. When True, it continues
2483        toward ``row - 1``, ``row - 2``, … instead.
2484
2485        Args:
2486            row: Starting data row index (0-based).
2487            column: Starting column index (0-based).
2488            columns: Number of columns in each filled row (band width, >= 1).
2489            items: Cell contents in fill order.
2490            from_bottom_left: If True, advance toward smaller data-row indices;
2491                if False, advance toward larger ones.
2492
2493        Returns:
2494            Self: This table.
2495
2496        Raises:
2497            ValueError: If ``columns`` is less than 1.
2498            IndexError: If a target row or column index is negative.
2499
2500        Examples:
2501            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2502            >>> table.populate(0, 0, 2, [1, 2, 3]) is table
2503            True
2504            >>> table.cell(1, 0).content
2505            1
2506            >>> table.cell(1, 1).content
2507            2
2508            >>> table.cell(2, 0).content
2509            3
2510            >>> table2 = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2511            >>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
2512            >>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
2513            >>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
2514            >>> _ = table2.populate(2, 0, 2, ["a", "b", "c"], from_bottom_left=True)
2515            >>> table2.cell(3, 0).content
2516            'a'
2517            >>> table2.cell(2, 0).content
2518            'c'
2519        """
2520        if columns < 1:
2521            raise ValueError("columns must be at least 1")
2522        if row < 0 or column < 0:
2523            raise IndexError("row or column index out of range")
2524        if not items:
2525            return self
2526
2527        item_count = len(items)
2528        local_rows = (item_count + columns - 1) // columns
2529        if from_bottom_left:
2530            min_data_row = row - (local_rows - 1)
2531            max_data_row = row
2532        else:
2533            min_data_row = row
2534            max_data_row = row + (local_rows - 1)
2535        if min_data_row < 0:
2536            raise IndexError("row index out of range")
2537        max_grid_col = column + columns - 1
2538        while len(self._columns) <= max_grid_col:
2539            self._append_column("")
2540        while len(self._rows) <= max_data_row:
2541            self.add_row(*([""] * len(self._columns)))
2542
2543        for index, item in enumerate(items):
2544            local_row = index // columns
2545            local_col = index % columns
2546            grid_col = column + local_col
2547            if from_bottom_left:
2548                data_row = row - local_row
2549            else:
2550                data_row = row + local_row
2551            grid_row = _grid_row_from_data_row(self, data_row)
2552            self._cell_at_grid(grid_row, grid_col).content = item
2553        return self
2554
2555    def _rich_style_from_cell(
2556        self,
2557        grid_row: int,
2558        col_index: int,
2559    ) -> RichStyle | None:
2560        fmt = _resolve_cell_format(self, grid_row, col_index)
2561        bg = _resolve_cell_background(self, grid_row, col_index)
2562        style_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
2563        if fmt.get("bold"):
2564            style_kwargs["bold"] = True
2565        if fmt.get("italic"):
2566            style_kwargs["italic"] = True
2567        if "font_color" in fmt:
2568            style_kwargs["color"] = _rich_color(fmt["font_color"])
2569        if bg.get("fill") and "fill_color" in bg:
2570            style_kwargs["bgcolor"] = _rich_color(bg["fill_color"])
2571        if not style_kwargs:
2572            return None
2573        return RichStyle(**style_kwargs)
2574
2575    def build_rich_table(self) -> RichTable:
2576        """Build a Rich ``Table`` for notebook display.
2577
2578        Examples:
2579            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2580            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
2581            >>> table.build_rich_table()  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
2582            <rich.table.Table object at ...>
2583        """
2584        rich_table = RichTable(
2585            title=self.title or None,
2586            show_header=False,
2587            show_lines=self.show_lines,
2588            min_width=self.min_width,
2589            padding=self.padding,
2590        )
2591        column_count = len(self._columns)
2592        has_header = _has_header_row(self)
2593        for col_index, column in enumerate(self._columns):
2594            fmt = _resolve_cell_format(self, 0, col_index)
2595            justify = _align_to_rich_justify(fmt["align"])
2596            rich_table.add_column(column.header, justify=justify)
2597        if has_header:
2598            from rich.text import Text
2599
2600            header_cells = []
2601            for col_index in range(column_count):
2602                style = self._rich_style_from_cell(0, col_index)
2603                text = self._columns[col_index].header
2604                if style is not None:
2605                    header_cells.append(Text(text, style=style))
2606                else:
2607                    header_cells.append(text)
2608            rich_table.add_row(*header_cells)
2609        grid_header_rows = 1 if has_header else 0
2610        for row_index, row in enumerate(self._rows):
2611            grid_row = row_index + grid_header_rows
2612            rich_cells = []
2613            from rich.text import Text
2614
2615            for col_index in range(column_count):
2616                cell = row.cells[col_index]
2617                text = _cell_display_text(cell.content)
2618                style = self._rich_style_from_cell(grid_row, col_index)
2619                if style is not None:
2620                    rich_cells.append(Text(text, style=style))
2621                else:
2622                    rich_cells.append(text)
2623            rich_table.add_row(*rich_cells)
2624        return rich_table
2625
2626    def display(self) -> None:
2627        """Show this table in a Jupyter cell using Rich.
2628
2629        Examples:
2630            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2631            >>> table.display()  # doctest: +SKIP
2632        """
2633        console = Console(force_jupyter=True)
2634        console.print(self.build_rich_table())
2635
2636    def _ipython_display_(self) -> None:
2637        """IPython hook: Rich table in notebook output."""
2638        self.display()
2639
2640    def drawable_cells(self) -> list[Any]:
2641        """Return drawable objects stored in cells (row-major).
2642
2643        Examples:
2644            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2645            >>> _ = table.add_row("text")
2646            >>> table.drawable_cells()
2647            []
2648        """
2649        drawables: list[Any] = []
2650        for row in self._rows:
2651            for cell in row.cells:
2652                content = cell.content
2653                if _is_drawable_content(content):
2654                    drawables.append(content)
2655        return drawables

141class SplitCell:
142    """Two labels in one table cell, separated by a divider.
143
144    This is cell *content*, not an unmerge operation. ``kind`` is a divider
145    character or a ``SplitCell`` class attribute (same strings).
146
147    ``"-"`` / ``HORIZONTAL``: ``first`` on top, ``second`` on bottom.
148    ``"|"`` / ``VERTICAL``: ``first`` on the left, ``second`` on the right.
149    ``"\\\\"`` / ``DIAGONAL_DOWN``: ``first`` lower-left, ``second`` upper-right.
150    ``"/"`` / ``DIAGONAL_UP``: ``first`` upper-left, ``second`` lower-right.
151
152    ``offset1`` and ``offset2`` are ``(dx, dy)`` added after that default
153    placement.
154
155    Examples:
156        >>> split = SplitCell(SplitCell.HORIZONTAL, "top", "bottom")
157        >>> split.kind
158        '-'
159        >>> split.second
160        'bottom'
161    """
162
163    HORIZONTAL = "-"
164    VERTICAL = "|"
165    DIAGONAL_UP = "/"
166    DIAGONAL_DOWN = "\\"
167
168    def __init__(
169        self,
170        kind: str,
171        first: str,
172        second: str,
173        offset1: PointType = (0.0, 0.0),
174        offset2: PointType = (0.0, 0.0),
175    ) -> None:
176        if kind not in _SPLIT_CELL_KINDS:
177            raise ValueError(
178                f"SplitCell kind must be one of {sorted(_SPLIT_CELL_KINDS)}"
179            )
180        self.kind = kind
181        self.first = first
182        self.second = second
183        self.offset1 = offset1
184        self.offset2 = offset2

197class Cell:
198    """One table cell: content plus local format and background overrides.
199
200    Examples:
201        >>> cell = Cell("value")
202        >>> cell.content
203        'value'
204    """
205
206    def __init__(self, content: Any = "") -> None:
207        """Create a cell.
208
209        Args:
210            content: Text, number, or drawable object.
211
212        Examples:
213            >>> Cell(42).content
214            42
215        """
216        object.__setattr__(self, "_layout_revision", 0)
217        self.content = content
218        self._format: dict[str, Any] = {}
219        self._background: dict[str, Any] = {}
220
221    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: Any) -> None:
222        object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
223        if name == "content" and "_layout_revision" in vars(self):
224            object.__setattr__(
225                self, "_layout_revision", self._layout_revision + 1
226            )
227
228    def set_format(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Self:
229        """Set cell styling (merged on top of row/column/table).
230
231        Content keys go to ``_format``. Background keys (``fill``,
232        ``fill_color``, ``fill_alpha``, ``stroke``, ``line_color``,
233        ``line_alpha``, ``line_width``) go to ``_background``, same as
234        ``cell.fill_color = ...``.
235
236        Examples:
237            >>> cell = Cell("x")
238            >>> cell.set_format(bold=True) is cell
239            True
240            >>> cell._format["bold"]
241            True
242            >>> _ = cell.set_format(fill=True, fill_color="gold")
243            >>> cell._background["fill"]
244            True
245        """
246        format_kwargs, background_kwargs = _split_style_kwargs(kwargs)
247        self._format.update(format_kwargs)
248        self._background.update(background_kwargs)
249        if format_kwargs:
250            object.__setattr__(
251                self, "_layout_revision", self._layout_revision + 1
252            )
253        return self
254
255    def set_background(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Self:
256        """Set background styling for this cell.
257
258        Examples:
259            >>> cell = Cell("x")
260            >>> _ = cell.set_background(fill=True)
261            >>> cell._background["fill"]
262            True
263        """
264        self._background.update(kwargs)
265        return self

534    """Rectangular grid region (inclusive bounds, 0-based grid indices).

536    **Grid coordinates:** ``row`` and ``col`` are integers starting at ``0``.
537    Column ``0`` is the leftmost column. Row numbering follows the table
538    origin: top-down by default, bottom-up when ``table.from_bottom_left`` is
539    True. The header row is included only when explicit headers are shown. This
540    matches :attr:`Table.cells`, :meth:`Table.range`, and :meth:`Table.cell`.
541
542    Single cell: ``table.range(r, c, r, c).cell`` or ``table.cells[r, c]``.
543
544    ``table.columns[i]`` / ``table.columns[i:j]`` slice **column indices**
545    ``0``, ``1``, … ``table.rows[i]`` slices **data rows** only (header
546    excluded); ``table.rows[0]`` is the first body row.
547
548    ``table.cells[row, col]`` is NumPy-style (grid row first). A lone index or
549    slice on ``table.cells`` selects grid rows and keeps all columns.
550
551    Assign format or background attributes on a range to apply them to every
552    cell in the range (column/row ranges also store the value on the
553    ``Column`` / ``Row`` so later rows inherit it).
554
555    Examples:
556        >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
557        >>> _ = table.add_row(1, 2)
558        >>> table.cells.font_size = 12
559        >>> table.cell(1, 0).content
560        1
561        >>> table.column(0).header
562        'A'
563"""
564
565    def __init__(
566        self,
567        table: Table,
568        row_start: int,
569        col_start: int,
570        row_end: int,
571        col_end: int,
572        *,
573        size_axis: Literal["columns", "rows"] | None = None,
574        explicit_grid_rows: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
575        explicit_grid_cols: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
576    ) -> None:
577        if row_start < 0 or row_end < 0 or col_start < 0 or col_end < 0:
578            object.__setattr__(self, "_table", table)
579            object.__setattr__(self, "_row_start", row_start)
580            object.__setattr__(self, "_row_end", row_end)
581            object.__setattr__(self, "_col_start", col_start)
582            object.__setattr__(self, "_col_end", col_end)
583            object.__setattr__(self, "_size_axis", size_axis)
584            object.__setattr__(self, "_explicit_grid_rows", None)
585            object.__setattr__(self, "_explicit_grid_cols", None)
586            return
587        object.__setattr__(self, "_table", table)
588        object.__setattr__(self, "_row_start", min(row_start, row_end))
589        object.__setattr__(self, "_row_end", max(row_start, row_end))
590        object.__setattr__(self, "_col_start", min(col_start, col_end))
591        object.__setattr__(self, "_col_end", max(col_start, col_end))
592        object.__setattr__(self, "_size_axis", size_axis)
593        object.__setattr__(self, "_explicit_grid_rows", explicit_grid_rows)
594        object.__setattr__(self, "_explicit_grid_cols", explicit_grid_cols)
595
596    def _empty_subrange(self) -> Range:
597        return Range(
598            self._table,
599            0,
600            0,
601            -1,
602            -1,
603            size_axis=self._size_axis,
604        )
605
606    def __getitem__(
607        self,
608        key: int | slice | tuple[int | slice, int | slice],
609    ) -> Range:
610        if self._size_axis == "columns":
611            if not isinstance(key, (int, slice)):
612                raise TypeError("columns range indices must be an int or slice")
613            col_base = (
614                list(self._explicit_grid_cols)
615                if self._explicit_grid_cols is not None
616                else None
617            )
618            picked_cols = _slice_pick_indices(
619                self._col_start,
620                self._col_end,
621                key,
622                base=col_base,
623            )
624            if not picked_cols:
625                return self._empty_subrange()
626            return Range(
627                self._table,
628                self._row_start,
629                picked_cols[0],
630                self._row_end,
631                picked_cols[-1],
632                size_axis="columns",
633                explicit_grid_rows=self._explicit_grid_rows,
634                explicit_grid_cols=_explicit_indices(picked_cols),
635            )
636        if self._size_axis == "rows":
637            if not isinstance(key, (int, slice)):
638                raise TypeError("rows range indices must be an int or slice")
639            row_base = (
640                list(self._explicit_grid_rows)
641                if self._explicit_grid_rows is not None
642                else None
643            )
644            picked_rows = _slice_pick_indices(
645                self._row_start,
646                self._row_end,
647                key,
648                base=row_base,
649            )
650            if not picked_rows:
651                return self._empty_subrange()
652            return Range(
653                self._table,
654                picked_rows[0],
655                self._col_start,
656                picked_rows[-1],
657                self._col_end,
658                size_axis="rows",
659                explicit_grid_rows=_explicit_indices(picked_rows),
660                explicit_grid_cols=self._explicit_grid_cols,
661            )
662        if isinstance(key, (int, slice)):
663            row_key: int | slice = key
664            col_key: int | slice = slice(None)
665        elif isinstance(key, tuple) and len(key) == 2:
666            row_key, col_key = key
667        else:
668            raise TypeError(
669                "cell range indices must be a row index/slice or a "
670                "(row, column) pair of ints or slices"
671            )
672        if not isinstance(row_key, (int, slice)) or not isinstance(
673            col_key, (int, slice)
674        ):
675            raise TypeError(
676                "cell range indices must be a row index/slice or a "
677                "(row, column) pair of ints or slices"
678            )
679        row_base = (
680            list(self._explicit_grid_rows)
681            if self._explicit_grid_rows is not None
682            else None
683        )
684        col_base = (
685            list(self._explicit_grid_cols)
686            if self._explicit_grid_cols is not None
687            else None
688        )
689        picked_rows = _slice_pick_indices(
690            self._row_start,
691            self._row_end,
692            row_key,
693            base=row_base,
694        )
695        picked_cols = _slice_pick_indices(
696            self._col_start,
697            self._col_end,
698            col_key,
699            base=col_base,
700        )
701        if not picked_rows or not picked_cols:
702            return Range(self._table, 0, 0, -1, -1)
703        return Range(
704            self._table,
705            picked_rows[0],
706            picked_cols[0],
707            picked_rows[-1],
708            picked_cols[-1],
709            explicit_grid_rows=_explicit_indices(picked_rows),
710            explicit_grid_cols=_explicit_indices(picked_cols),
711        )
712
713    def _is_empty(self) -> bool:
714        return (
715            self._row_end < self._row_start or self._col_end < self._col_start
716        )
717
718    def _grid_row_indices(self) -> list[int]:
719        if self._is_empty():
720            return []
721        if self._explicit_grid_rows is not None:
722            return list(self._explicit_grid_rows)
723        return list(range(self._row_start, self._row_end + 1))
724
725    def _grid_col_indices(self) -> list[int]:
726        if self._is_empty():
727            return []
728        if self._explicit_grid_cols is not None:
729            return list(self._explicit_grid_cols)
730        return list(range(self._col_start, self._col_end + 1))
731
732    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
733        if name == "width":
734            return self._common_column_width()
735        if name == "height":
736            return self._common_row_height()
737        if name == "size":
738            return (self.width, self.height)
739        target = _range_style_target(name)
740        if target is None:
741            raise AttributeError(
742                f"'{type(self).__name__}' object has no attribute '{name}'"
743            )
744        _kind, storage_name = target
745        return self._style_value(storage_name, _kind)
746
747    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: Any) -> None:
748        if name.startswith("_"):
749            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
750            return
751        if name == "content":
752            self.cell.content = value
753            return
754        if name == "width":
755            self._assign_width(value)
756            return
757        if name == "height":
758            self._assign_height(value)
759            return
760        if name == "size":
761            width, height = value[:2]
762            self._assign_width(width)
763            self._assign_height(height)
764            return
765        target = _range_style_target(name)
766        if target is None:
767            raise AttributeError(
768                f"'{type(self).__name__}' object has no attribute '{name}'"
769            )
770        kind, storage_name = target
771        if storage_name in ("align", "v_align"):
772            value = _resolve_align(value)
773        self._apply_style(kind, storage_name, value)
774
775    def _style_store(self, cell: Cell, kind: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
776        if kind == "format":
777            return cell._format
778        return cell._background
779
780    def _style_value(self, storage_name: str, kind: str) -> Any:
781        first = None
782        saw_value = False
783        for cell in self:
784            store = self._style_store(cell, kind)
785            if storage_name not in store:
786                return None
787            current = store[storage_name]
788            if not saw_value:
789                first = current
790                saw_value = True
791            elif current != first:
792                return None
793        if not saw_value:
794            return None
795        return first
796
797    def _apply_style(self, kind: str, storage_name: str, value: Any) -> None:
798        if self._is_empty():
799            raise ValueError("assignment on an empty range")
800        kwargs = {storage_name: value}
801        if self._size_axis == "columns":
802            for col_index in self._grid_col_indices():
803                column = self._table._columns[col_index]
804                if kind == "format":
805                    column.set_format(**kwargs)
806                else:
807                    column.set_background(**kwargs)
808            return
809        if self._size_axis == "rows":
810            header_rows = 1 if _has_header_row(self._table) else 0
811            for grid_row in self._grid_row_indices():
812                data_row = grid_row - header_rows
813                row = self._table._rows[data_row]
814                if kind == "format":
815                    row.set_format(**kwargs)
816                else:
817                    row.set_background(**kwargs)
818            return
819        if kind == "format":
820            self.set_format(**kwargs)
821        else:
822            self.set_background(**kwargs)
823
824    @property
825    def cell(self) -> Cell:
826        """The sole cell when this range is one grid cell.
827
828        Examples:
829            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
830            >>> _ = table.add_row("v")
831            >>> table.range(1, 0, 1, 0).cell.content
832            'v'
833        """
834        if self._row_start != self._row_end or self._col_start != self._col_end:
835            raise ValueError("cell is only defined for a single-cell range")
836        return self._table._cell_at_grid(self._row_start, self._col_start)
837
838    @property
839    def content(self) -> Any:
840        """Content of a single-cell range.
841
842        Examples:
843            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
844            >>> _ = table.add_row(7)
845            >>> table.range(1, 0, 1, 0).content
846            7
847        """
848        return self.cell.content
849
850    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Cell]:
851        for grid_row in self._grid_row_indices():
852            for col_index in self._grid_col_indices():
853                yield self._table._cell_at_grid(grid_row, col_index)
854
855    @property
856    def cells(self) -> list[list[Cell]]:
857        """Cell matrix for this range (rows, then columns).
858
859        Examples:
860            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
861            >>> _ = table.add_row(1, 2)
862            >>> len(table.cells.cells)
863            2
864        """
865        matrix: list[list[Cell]] = []
866        for grid_row in self._grid_row_indices():
867            row_cells: list[Cell] = []
868            for col_index in self._grid_col_indices():
869                row_cells.append(  # noqa: PERF401
870                    self._table._cell_at_grid(grid_row, col_index)
871                )
872            matrix.append(row_cells)
873        return matrix
874
875    def set_format(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Self:
876        """Apply format to every cell in this range.
877
878        Examples:
879            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
880            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
881            >>> _ = table.rows.set_format(bold=True)
882            >>> table.cell(1, 0)._format["bold"]
883            True
884        """
885        for cell in self:
886            cell.set_format(**kwargs)
887        return self
888
889    def set_background(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Self:
890        """Apply background to every cell in this range.
891
892        Examples:
893            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
894            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
895            >>> _ = table.rows.set_background(fill=True)
896            >>> table.cell(1, 0)._background["fill"]
897            True
898        """
899        for cell in self:
900            cell.set_background(**kwargs)
901        return self
902
903    def _assign_width(self, width: float | Sequence[float]) -> None:
904        if self._is_empty():
905            raise ValueError("width assignment on an empty range")
906        self._table._apply_column_widths(
907            self._col_start, self._col_end, width
908        )
909
910    def _assign_height(self, height: float | Sequence[float]) -> None:
911        if self._is_empty():
912            raise ValueError("height assignment on an empty range")
913        grid_rows = self._grid_row_indices()
914        if (
915            self._explicit_grid_rows is None
916            and len(grid_rows) == self._row_end - self._row_start + 1
917        ):
918            self._table._apply_grid_row_heights(
919                self._row_start, self._row_end, height
920            )
921            return
922        for grid_row, row_height in zip(
923            grid_rows,
924            self._table._sizes_for_span(len(grid_rows), height, kind="row"),
925            strict=True,
926        ):
927            if _has_header_row(self._table) and grid_row == 0:
928                self._table._header_row_height = row_height
929            else:
930                data_row = grid_row - (1 if _has_header_row(self._table) else 0)
931                self._table._rows[data_row]._height = row_height
932        self._table._invalidate_layout()
933
934    def _common_column_width(self) -> float | None:
935        first = None
936        saw_value = False
937        for col_index in self._grid_col_indices():
938            current = self._table._columns[col_index]._width
939            if not saw_value:
940                first = current
941                saw_value = True
942            elif current != first:
943                return None
944        if not saw_value:
945            return None
946        return first
947
948    def _stored_grid_row_height(self, grid_row: int) -> float | None:
949        table = self._table
950        if _has_header_row(table) and grid_row == 0:
951            return table._header_row_height
952        data_row = grid_row - (1 if _has_header_row(table) else 0)
953        return table._rows[data_row]._height
954
955    def _common_row_height(self) -> float | None:
956        first = None
957        saw_value = False
958        for grid_row in self._grid_row_indices():
959            current = self._stored_grid_row_height(grid_row)
960            if not saw_value:
961                first = current
962                saw_value = True
963            elif current != first:
964                return None
965        if not saw_value:
966            return None
967        return first

969    @property
970    def b_box(self) -> BoundingBox:
971        """Axis-aligned box enclosing this range.
972
973        Examples:
974            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
975            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
976            >>> table.cells.b_box.width > 0
977            True
978        """
979        boxes = [
980            table_cell_bbox(self._table, grid_row, col_index)
981            for grid_row in self._grid_row_indices()
982            for col_index in self._grid_col_indices()
983        ]
984        return _union_bounding_boxes(boxes)

Rectangular grid region (inclusive bounds, 0-based grid indices).

Grid coordinates: row and col are integers starting at 0. Column 0 is the leftmost column. Row numbering follows the table origin: top-down by default, bottom-up when table.from_bottom_left is True. The header row is included only when explicit headers are shown. This matches Table.cells, Table.range(), and Table.cell().

Single cell: table.range(r, c, r, c).cell or table.cells[r, c].

table.columns[i] / table.columns[i:j] slice column indices 0, 1, … table.rows[i] slices data rows only (header excluded); table.rows[0] is the first body row.

table.cells[row, col] is NumPy-style (grid row first). A lone index or slice on table.cells selects grid rows and keeps all columns.

Assign format or background attributes on a range to apply them to every cell in the range (column/row ranges also store the value on the Column / Row so later rows inherit it).

Examples:
>>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
>>> _ = table.add_row(1, 2)
>>> table.cells.font_size = 12
>>> table.cell(1, 0).content
1
>>> table.column(0).header
'A'

1230    table: Table,
1231) -> tuple[list[float], list[float], int]:
1232    """Return column widths, row heights, and column count for ``table``.
1233
1234    Examples:
1235        >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
1236        >>> _ = table.add_row(1, 22)
1237        >>> widths, heights, n_cols = compute_table_layout(table)
1238        >>> n_cols
1239        2
1240        >>> len(widths)
1241        2
1242        >>> len(heights)
1243        2
1244        >>> square = Table(size=(2, 2), column_width=30, row_height=30, padding=0)
1245        >>> compute_table_layout(square)
1246        ([30, 30], [30, 30], 2)
1247    """
1248    cache_key = _table_layout_cache_key(table)
1249    if (
1250        table._layout_cache_key == cache_key
1251        and table._layout_cache is not None
1252    ):
1253        cached_widths, cached_heights, cached_column_count = (
1254            table._layout_cache
1255        )
1256        return (
1257            list(cached_widths),
1258            list(cached_heights),
1259            cached_column_count,
1260        )
1261
1262    column_count, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(table)
1263    if column_count == 0:
1264        return [], [], 0
1265
1266    col_widths = [0.0] * column_count
1267    row_heights = [0.0] * grid_row_count
1268
1269    padding_x, padding_y = _table_padding_xy(table)
1270    pad_x = 2 * padding_x
1271    pad_y = 2 * padding_y
1272    has_header = _has_header_row(table)
1273
1274    for grid_row in range(grid_row_count):
1275        for col_index in range(column_count):
1276            fmt = _resolve_cell_format(table, grid_row, col_index)
1277            if has_header and grid_row == 0:
1278                content = table._columns[col_index].header_cell.content
1279            else:
1280                data_row = grid_row - (1 if has_header else 0)
1281                content = table._rows[data_row].cells[col_index].content
1282            content_w, content_h = _cell_content_size(content, fmt)
1283            col_widths[col_index] = max(
1284                col_widths[col_index], content_w + pad_x
1285            )
1286            row_heights[grid_row] = max(
1287                row_heights[grid_row], content_h + pad_y
1288            )
1289
1290    for col_index in range(column_count):
1291        width = table._columns[col_index]._width
1292        if width is not None:
1293            col_widths[col_index] = max(col_widths[col_index], width)
1294
1295    for grid_row in range(grid_row_count):
1296        if has_header and grid_row == 0:
1297            header_height = table._header_row_height
1298            if header_height is not None:
1299                row_heights[grid_row] = max(
1300                    row_heights[grid_row], header_height
1301                )
1302        else:
1303            data_row = grid_row - (1 if has_header else 0)
1304            height = table._rows[data_row]._height
1305            if height is not None:
1306                row_heights[grid_row] = max(row_heights[grid_row], height)
1307
1308    if table.min_width is not None:
1309        total = sum(col_widths)
1310        if total < table.min_width and column_count:
1311            extra = (table.min_width - total) / column_count
1312            col_widths = [width + extra for width in col_widths]
1313
1314    table._layout_cache_key = cache_key
1315    table._layout_cache = (
1316        tuple(col_widths),
1317        tuple(row_heights),
1318        column_count,
1319    )
1320
1321    return col_widths, row_heights, column_count

Return column widths, row heights, and column count for table.

Examples:
>>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
>>> _ = table.add_row(1, 22)
>>> widths, heights, n_cols = compute_table_layout(table)
>>> n_cols
2
>>> len(widths)
2
>>> len(heights)
2
>>> square = Table(size=(2, 2), column_width=30, row_height=30, padding=0)
>>> compute_table_layout(square)
([30, 30], [30, 30], 2)

def build_table_sketch( table: Table, canvas: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> simetri.render.sketch.TableSketch: 
1670def build_table_sketch(table: Table, canvas: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> TableSketch:
1671    """Lay out ``table`` and return a ``TableSketch`` for SVG/PDF export.
1672
1673    Examples:
1674        >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
1675        >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
1676        >>> build_table_sketch.__name__
1677        'build_table_sketch'
1678    """
1679    col_widths, row_heights, column_count = compute_table_layout(table)
1680    pos = table.pos[:2]
1681    sketches: list = []
1682    grid_row_count = len(row_heights)
1683    padding_x, padding_y = _table_padding_xy(table)
1684
1685    if table.title:
1686        title_y = pos[1] + _TABLE_DEFAULT_TITLE_PAD
1687        title_tag = Tag(
1688            table.title,
1689            (pos[0], title_y),
1690            font_size=table.font_size + 2,
1691            bold=True,
1692            anchor=Anchor.WEST,
1693            align=Align.LEFT,
1694        )
1695        sketches.extend(get_sketches(title_tag, canvas, **kwargs))
1696        pos = (pos[0], pos[1] - _TABLE_DEFAULT_TITLE_PAD - table.font_size)
1697
1698    for grid_row in range(grid_row_count):
1699        for col_index in range(column_count):
1700            background = _resolve_cell_background(table, grid_row, col_index)
1701            x_left, y_top, x_right, y_bottom = _cell_box(
1702                pos, col_widths, row_heights, grid_row, col_index
1703            )
1704            sketches.extend(
1705                _background_rect_sketch(
1706                    canvas, x_left, y_top, x_right, y_bottom, background
1707                )
1708            )
1709
1710    if table.show_lines and column_count and row_heights:
1711        sketches.extend(
1712            _grid_line_sketches(table, canvas, pos, col_widths, row_heights)
1713        )
1714
1715    has_header = _has_header_row(table)
1716    for grid_row in range(grid_row_count):
1717        for col_index in range(column_count):
1718            fmt = _resolve_cell_format(table, grid_row, col_index)
1719            h_align = _resolve_align(fmt["align"])
1720            v_align = _resolve_align(
1721                fmt.get("v_align", _TABLE_DEFAULT_ROW_ALIGN)
1722            )
1723            x_left, y_top, x_right, y_bottom = _cell_box(
1724                pos, col_widths, row_heights, grid_row, col_index
1725            )
1726            cell_pos = _cell_anchor_pos(
1727                x_left,
1728                y_top,
1729                x_right,
1730                y_bottom,
1731                h_align,
1732                v_align,
1733                padding_x,
1734                padding_y,
1735            )
1736            if has_header and grid_row == 0:
1737                content = table._columns[col_index].header_cell.content
1738            else:
1739                data_row = grid_row - (1 if has_header else 0)
1740                content = table._rows[data_row].cells[col_index].content
1741            if isinstance(content, Cell):
1742                content = content.content
1743            if isinstance(content, SplitCell):
1744                sketches.extend(
1745                    _split_cell_sketches(
1746                        content,
1747                        canvas,
1748                        x_left,
1749                        y_top,
1750                        x_right,
1751                        y_bottom,
1752                        fmt,
1753                        padding_x,
1754                        padding_y,
1755                        **kwargs,
1756                    )
1757                )
1758            elif _is_drawable_content(content):
1759                midpoint_x, midpoint_y = content.midpoint[:2]
1760                dest_x, dest_y = cell_pos[:2]
1761                shift_x = dest_x - midpoint_x
1762                shift_y = dest_y - midpoint_y
1763                base_sketch_xform = canvas._sketch_xform_matrix
1764                canvas._sketch_xform_matrix = (
1765                    translation_matrix(shift_x, shift_y) @ base_sketch_xform
1766                )
1767                try:
1768                    cell_sketches = get_sketches(content, canvas, **kwargs)
1769                finally:
1770                    canvas._sketch_xform_matrix = base_sketch_xform
1771
1772                sketches.extend(_flatten_sketches(cell_sketches))
1773            else:
1774                tag = _tag_for_content(content, cell_pos, fmt)
1775                sketches.extend(get_sketches(tag, canvas, **kwargs))
1776
1777    return TableSketch(
1778        pos=pos,
1779        column_widths=col_widths,
1780        row_heights=row_heights,
1781        sketches=sketches,
1782        show_lines=table.show_lines,
1783        xform_matrix=canvas._sketch_xform_matrix,
1784    )

Lay out table and return a TableSketch for SVG/PDF export.

Examples:
>>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
>>> _ = table.add_row("x")
>>> build_table_sketch.__name__
'build_table_sketch'
class Table: 
1787class Table:
1788    """Documentation table with Rich notebook and vector export.
1789
1790    **Cell indexing:** 0-based column indices ``0``, ``1``, … everywhere.
1791    Use **grid rows** for :attr:`cells`, :meth:`range`, and :meth:`cell`
1792    (row ``0`` is the header when a header is shown; the next row is ``1``).
1793    Use **data rows** for :meth:`row` and :meth:`populate` (row ``0`` is the
1794    first body row). See the module docstring for the full convention.
1795    Header strings in ``columns=["A", "B"]`` are display labels only — not
1796    column coordinates.
1797
1798    Examples:
1799        >>> table = Table(
1800        ...     title="Parameters",
1801        ...     columns=["Name", "Value"],
1802        ...     size=(2, 2),
1803        ...     column_align=[Align.LEFT, Align.RIGHT],
1804        ... )
1805        >>> table.cell(1, 0).content = "n_sides"
1806        >>> table.cell(1, 1).content = 7
1807        >>> table.cell(2, 0).content = "skip"
1808        >>> table.cell(2, 1).content = 3
1809        >>> table.build_rich_table()  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
1810        <rich.table.Table object at ...>
1811"""
1812
1813    def __init__(
1814        self,
1815        title: str = _TABLE_DEFAULT_TITLE,
1816        columns: Sequence[str] | None = None,
1817        *,
1818        size: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
1819        from_bottom_left: bool = False,
1820        pos: PointType = _TABLE_DEFAULT_POS,
1821        show_header: bool = _TABLE_DEFAULT_SHOW_HEADER,
1822        show_lines: bool = _TABLE_DEFAULT_SHOW_LINES,
1823        column_align: Sequence[Align | str] | None = None,
1824        column_width: float | None = None,
1825        min_width: int | None = _TABLE_DEFAULT_MIN_WIDTH,
1826        padding: tuple[int, int] = _TABLE_DEFAULT_PADDING,
1827        font_size: float = _TABLE_DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE,
1828        row_height: float | None = None,
1829    ) -> None:
1830        """Create an empty table with optional column headers and size.
1831
1832        Args:
1833            title: Table title for notebook and vector output.
1834            columns: Optional column header labels.
1835            size: Optional ``(rows, columns)`` body size to pre-create.
1836            from_bottom_left: Whether row indexing starts at the bottom.
1837            pos: Northwest table position.
1838            show_header: Whether to show the header row.
1839            show_lines: Whether to stroke grid lines.
1840            column_align: Optional per-column alignment list.
1841            column_width: Default width applied to created columns.
1842            min_width: Minimum total table width after layout.
1843            padding: Cell padding for vector layout and Rich preview.
1844            font_size: Base font size.
1845            row_height: Default height applied to created rows.
1846
1847        Raises:
1848            ValueError: If ``size`` is not two non-negative integers, or if
1849                ``columns`` has more labels than ``size[1]``.
1850
1851        Examples:
1852            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1853            >>> table = sg.Table(size=(2, 3))
1854            >>> len(table._rows), len(table._columns)
1855            (2, 3)
1856            >>> bottom = sg.Table(size=(2, 1), from_bottom_left=True)
1857            >>> bottom.cell(0, 0).content = "south"
1858            >>> bottom.cell(1, 0).content = "north"
1859            >>> bottom.row(0).cells[0].content
1860            'south'
1861            >>> no_headers = sg.Table(size=(1, 1))
1862            >>> len(no_headers.cells.cells)
1863            1
1864            >>> sized = sg.Table(columns=["A", "B"], size=(1, 3))
1865            >>> sized.column_headers
1866            ['A', 'B', '']
1867        """
1868        self._layout_cache: (
1869            tuple[tuple[float, ...], tuple[float, ...], int] | None
1870        ) = None
1871        self._layout_cache_key: tuple[Any, ...] | None = None
1872        self._layout_revision = 0
1873        self.title = title
1874        self.pos = pos
1875        self.type = Types.TABLE
1876        self.subtype = Types.TABLE
1877        self.visible = True
1878        self.from_bottom_left = from_bottom_left
1879        self.show_header = show_header
1880        self.show_lines = show_lines
1881        self._explicit_headers = False
1882        self.min_width = min_width
1883        self.padding = padding
1884        self.font_size = font_size
1885        self._format: dict[str, Any] = {"font_size": font_size}
1886        self._background: dict[str, Any] = {}
1887        self._columns: list[Column] = []
1888        self._rows: list[Row] = []
1889        self._default_column_width = column_width
1890        self._default_row_height = row_height
1891        self._header_row_height: float | None = row_height
1892
1893        row_count = 0
1894        target_column_count = 0
1895        if size is not None:
1896            if len(size) != 2:
1897                raise ValueError("size must be a (rows, columns) tuple")
1898            row_count, target_column_count = size
1899            if (
1900                type(row_count) is not int
1901                or type(target_column_count) is not int
1902                or row_count < 0
1903                or target_column_count < 0
1904            ):
1905                raise ValueError(
1906                    "size must contain two non-negative integers"
1907                )
1908
1909        if (
1910            size is not None
1911            and columns is not None
1912            and len(columns) > target_column_count
1913        ):
1914            raise ValueError(
1915                "columns has more labels than the requested size columns"
1916            )
1917
1918        explicit_headers = list(columns) if columns is not None else []
1919        headers = list(explicit_headers)
1920        if target_column_count > len(headers):
1921            headers.extend([""] * (target_column_count - len(headers)))
1922
1923        if explicit_headers:
1924            self._explicit_headers = True
1925        if headers:
1926            aligns = (
1927                list(column_align)
1928                if column_align is not None
1929                else [_TABLE_DEFAULT_COLUMN_ALIGN] * len(headers)
1930            )
1931            for index, header in enumerate(headers):
1932                align = (
1933                    aligns[index]
1934                    if index < len(aligns)
1935                    else _TABLE_DEFAULT_COLUMN_ALIGN
1936                )
1937                column = self._append_column(header)
1938                column.set_format(align=align)
1939
1940        for _ in range(row_count):
1941            self.add_row(*([""] * len(self._columns)))
1942
1943    def __repr__(self) -> str:
1944        """Return a Table string from this table's title.
1945
1946        Examples:
1947            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1948            >>> repr(sg.Table(title="Parameters"))
1949            "Table(title='Parameters')"
1950        """
1951        return f"Table(title={self.title!r})"
1952
1953    @property
1954    def columns(self) -> Range:
1955        """``Range`` over the grid; ``width`` sets column widths.
1956
1957        Examples:
1958            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
1959            >>> table.columns._size_axis
1960            'columns'
1961        """
1962        column_count, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
1963        if column_count == 0 or grid_row_count == 0:
1964            return Range(self, 0, 0, -1, -1, size_axis="columns")
1965        public_rows = tuple(_public_full_grid_rows(self))
1966        return Range(
1967            self,
1968            0,
1969            0,
1970            grid_row_count - 1,
1971            column_count - 1,
1972            size_axis="columns",
1973            explicit_grid_rows=public_rows,
1974        )
1975
1976    @property
1977    def column_headers(self) -> list[str]:
1978        """Column header labels.
1979
1980        Examples:
1981            >>> Table(columns=["X", "Y"]).column_headers
1982            ['X', 'Y']
1983        """
1984        return [column.header for column in self._columns]
1985
1986    @property
1987    def rows(self) -> Range:
1988        """``Range`` over data rows; ``height`` sets row heights.
1989
1990        ``table.rows[i]`` uses **data-row** indices: ``0`` is the first body
1991        row at the current origin (top by default, bottom when
1992        ``from_bottom_left`` is True). This differs from ``table.cells[i, …]``,
1993        which uses **grid-row** indices.
1994
1995        Examples:
1996            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
1997            >>> _ = table.add_row(1)
1998            >>> table.rows._size_axis
1999            'rows'
2000        """
2001        column_count, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
2002        if column_count == 0:
2003            return Range(self, 0, 0, -1, -1, size_axis="rows")
2004        public_rows = _public_body_grid_rows(self)
2005        if not public_rows:
2006            return Range(self, 0, 0, -1, -1, size_axis="rows")
2007        return Range(
2008            self,
2009            public_rows[0],
2010            0,
2011            public_rows[-1],
2012            column_count - 1,
2013            size_axis="rows",
2014            explicit_grid_rows=tuple(public_rows),
2015        )
2016
2017    @property
2018    def cells(self) -> Range:
2019        """``Range`` over the full grid (header row included when present).
2020
2021        Index as ``table.cells[grid_row, col]`` — both axes 0-based **grid**
2022        indices. Row numbering follows the table origin. With explicit headers
2023        and ``show_header=True``, the header is row ``0`` only when
2024        ``from_bottom_left`` is False; with ``from_bottom_left=True`` the header
2025        is the last grid row. For body-only row numbers use :meth:`cell` or
2026        :meth:`populate` instead.
2027
2028        Examples:
2029            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2030            >>> _ = table.add_row("z")
2031            >>> table.cells[0, 0].content
2032            'A'
2033            >>> table.cells[1, 0].content
2034            'z'
2035            >>> table.cell(1, 0).content
2036            'z'
2037        """
2038        column_count, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
2039        if column_count == 0 or grid_row_count == 0:
2040            return _empty_grid_range(self)
2041        public_rows = tuple(_public_full_grid_rows(self))
2042        return Range(
2043            self,
2044            0,
2045            0,
2046            grid_row_count - 1,
2047            column_count - 1,
2048            explicit_grid_rows=public_rows,
2049        )
2050
2051    def range(
2052        self,
2053        row_start: int,
2054        col_start: int,
2055        row_end: int,
2056        col_end: int,
2057    ) -> Range:
2058        """Return an inclusive rectangular region (0-based grid indices).
2059
2060        Same row/column convention as :attr:`cells`: grid row ``0`` is the
2061        first row at the current origin. The header is included only when
2062        explicit headers exist and ``show_header`` is True. Column indices start
2063        at ``0``.
2064
2065        Args:
2066            row_start: Top grid row of the range.
2067            col_start: Left column index.
2068            row_end: Bottom grid row of the range.
2069            col_end: Right column index.
2070
2071        Examples:
2072            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2073            >>> _ = table.add_row(1, 2)
2074            >>> table.range(1, 0, 1, 0).content
2075            1
2076        """
2077        public_rows = _public_full_grid_rows(self)
2078        start = min(row_start, row_end)
2079        end = max(row_start, row_end)
2080        picked_rows = public_rows[start : end + 1]
2081        return Range(
2082            self,
2083            picked_rows[0],
2084            col_start,
2085            picked_rows[-1],
2086            col_end,
2087            explicit_grid_rows=tuple(picked_rows),
2088        )
2089
2090    def _sizes_for_span(
2091        self,
2092        span: int,
2093        size: float | Sequence[float],
2094        *,
2095        kind: str,
2096    ) -> list[float]:
2097        if isinstance(size, Sequence) and not isinstance(size, (str, bytes)):
2098            values = list(size)
2099            if len(values) != span:
2100                raise ValueError(
2101                    f"{kind} size sequence length {len(values)} "
2102                    f"does not match range span {span}"
2103                )
2104            return values
2105        return [float(size)] * span
2106
2107    def _apply_column_widths(
2108        self,
2109        col_start: int,
2110        col_end: int,
2111        size: float | Sequence[float],
2112    ) -> None:
2113        span = col_end - col_start + 1
2114        if span <= 0:
2115            raise ValueError("width assignment on an empty range")
2116        for col_index, width in zip(
2117            range(col_start, col_end + 1),
2118            self._sizes_for_span(span, size, kind="column"),
2119            strict=True,
2120        ):
2121            self._columns[col_index]._width = width
2122        self._invalidate_layout()
2123
2124    def _apply_grid_row_heights(
2125        self,
2126        row_start: int,
2127        row_end: int,
2128        size: float | Sequence[float],
2129    ) -> None:
2130        span = row_end - row_start + 1
2131        if span <= 0:
2132            raise ValueError("height assignment on an empty range")
2133        for grid_row, height in zip(
2134            range(row_start, row_end + 1),
2135            self._sizes_for_span(span, size, kind="row"),
2136            strict=True,
2137        ):
2138            if _has_header_row(self) and grid_row == 0:
2139                self._header_row_height = height
2140            else:
2141                data_row = grid_row - (1 if _has_header_row(self) else 0)
2142                self._rows[data_row]._height = height
2143        self._invalidate_layout()
2144
2145    def _cell_at_grid(self, grid_row: int, col_index: int) -> Cell:
2146        column_count, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
2147        if col_index < 0 or col_index >= column_count:
2148            raise IndexError(f"column index {col_index} out of range")
2149        if grid_row < 0 or grid_row >= grid_row_count:
2150            raise IndexError(f"grid row {grid_row} out of range")
2151        if _has_header_row(self) and grid_row == 0:
2152            return self._columns[col_index].header_cell
2153        data_row = grid_row - (1 if _has_header_row(self) else 0)
2154        return self._rows[data_row].cells[col_index]

2156    def cell(self, row_index: int, col_index: int) -> Cell:
2157        """Return the cell at ``(row_index, col_index)``.
2158
2159        Row ``0`` is the header when a header row is shown. The next row is
2160        ``1``. With no header, row ``0`` is the first body row.
2161        ``col_index`` ``0`` is the leftmost column.
2162
2163        Examples:
2164            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2165            >>> _ = table.add_row("v")
2166            >>> table.cell(0, 0).content
2167            'A'
2168            >>> table.cell(1, 0).content
2169            'v'
2170        """
2171        if _has_header_row(self):
2172            return self._cell_at_grid(row_index, col_index)
2173        storage_index = _storage_row_index(self, row_index)
2174        return self._rows[storage_index].cells[col_index]

2198    def set_format(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Self:
2199        """Apply format to the table and every cell (including headers).
2200

2202            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2203            >>> _ = table.set_format(font_size=14)
2204            >>> table.font_size
2205            14
2206        """
2207        self._format.update(kwargs)
2208        if "font_size" in kwargs:
2209            object.__setattr__(self, "font_size", kwargs["font_size"])
2210        for column in self._columns:
2211            column.set_format(**kwargs)
2212        for row in self._rows:
2213            row.set_format(**kwargs)

2223            >>> table._background["fill"]

2233    def reset(self) -> Self:
2234        """Empty all cells and clear table, row, column, and cell styling.
2235
2236        The table keeps its current row and column counts, title, position,
2237        and visibility settings. Header labels are cleared because header cells
2238        are part of the grid.
2239
2240        Examples:
2241            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2242            >>> table = sg.Table(columns=["A"], size=(1, 1))
2243            >>> table.cell(0, 0).content = "x"
2244            >>> _ = table.column(0).set_format(align=sg.Align.RIGHT)
2245            >>> table.rows.height = 24
2246            >>> table.reset() is table
2247            True
2248            >>> table.column_headers
2249            ['']
2250            >>> table.cell(0, 0).content
2251            ''
2252            >>> table.column(0)._format
2253            {}
2254            >>> table.row(0)._height is None
2255            True
2256        """
2257        self.font_size = _TABLE_DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE
2258        self._format = {}
2259        self._background = {}
2260        self._header_row_height = self._default_row_height
2261
2262        for column in self._columns:
2263            column._format = {}
2264            column._background = {}
2265            column._width = self._default_column_width
2266            column.header = ""
2267            column.header_cell._format = {}
2268            column.header_cell._background = {}
2269
2270        for row in self._rows:
2271            row._format = {}
2272            row._background = {}
2273            row._height = self._default_row_height
2274            for cell in row.cells:
2275                cell.content = ""
2276                cell._format = {}
2277                cell._background = {}
2278
2279        self._invalidate_layout()
2280        return self

2282    def _invalidate_layout(self) -> None:
2283        object.__setattr__(self, "_layout_revision", self._layout_revision + 1)
2284        object.__setattr__(self, "_layout_cache_key", None)
2285        object.__setattr__(self, "_layout_cache", None)

2287    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
2288        target = _range_style_target(name)
2289        if target is None:
2290            raise AttributeError(
2291                f"'{type(self).__name__}' object has no attribute '{name}'"
2292            )
2293        kind, storage_name = target
2294        store = self._format if kind == "format" else self._background
2295        if storage_name not in store:
2296            return None
2297        return store[storage_name]

2299    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: Any) -> None:
2300        if name.startswith("_"):
2301            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
2302            return
2303        if "_format" not in vars(self):
2304            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
2305            return
2306        target = _range_style_target(name)
2307        if target is None:
2308            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
2309            if name in {"min_width", "padding", "show_header"}:
2310                self._invalidate_layout()
2311            return
2312        kind, storage_name = target
2313        if storage_name in ("align", "v_align"):
2314            value = _resolve_align(value)
2315        if kind == "format":
2316            self.set_format(**{storage_name: value})
2317            return
2318        self.set_background(**{storage_name: value})

2320    @property
2321    def b_box(self) -> BoundingBox:
2322        """Axis-aligned box enclosing the grid and optional title.
2323
2324        Examples:
2325            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2326            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
2327            >>> table.b_box.width > 0
2328            True

2330        boxes = [table_grid_bbox(self)]

2336    def _column_bbox(self, col_index: int) -> BoundingBox:
2337        _, row_heights, column_count = compute_table_layout(self)
2338        if col_index >= column_count:
2339            return BoundingBox()
2340        boxes = [
2341            table_cell_bbox(self, grid_row, col_index)
2342            for grid_row in range(len(row_heights))
2343        ]

2346    def _row_bbox(self, row_index: int) -> BoundingBox:

2348        grid_row = _grid_row_from_data_row(self, row_index)
2349        if grid_row >= len(row_heights):
2350            return BoundingBox()
2351        boxes = [
2352            table_cell_bbox(self, grid_row, col_index)
2353            for col_index in range(column_count)

2357    @property
2358    def corners(self) -> list[PointType]:
2359        """Bounding quadrilateral of the full table (northwest first).
2360
2361        Examples:
2362            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2363            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
2364            >>> len(table.corners)
2365            4
2366        """
2367        box = self.b_box
2368        if box.southwest is None:
2369            x, y = self.pos[:2]
2370            return [(x, y), (x, y), (x, y), (x, y)]
2371        return [
2372            box.northwest,
2373            box.northeast,
2374            box.southeast,
2375            box.southwest,
2376        ]

2378    @property
2379    def all_vertices(self) -> list[PointType]:

2383            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2384            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
2385            >>> len(table.all_vertices) >= 4
2386            True
2387        """

2389        if box.southwest is None:

2391            return [(x, y)]
