2394    def _append_column(self, header: str) -> Column:
2395        column = Column(self, len(self._columns), header)
2396        column._width = self._default_column_width
2397        self._columns.append(column)
2398        for row in self._rows:
2399            while len(row.cells) < len(self._columns):
2400                row.cells.append(Cell(""))
2401        self._invalidate_layout()
2402        return column

2404    def add_column(
2405        self,
2406        header: str,
2407        align: Align | str = _TABLE_DEFAULT_COLUMN_ALIGN,
2408    ) -> Column:
2409        """Append a column and return its ``Column`` object.
2410
2411        Examples:
2412            >>> table = Table()
2413            >>> col = table.add_column("New")
2414            >>> col.header
2415            'New'
2416        """
2417        self._explicit_headers = True
2418        column = self._append_column(header)
2419        column.set_format(align=align)
2420        return column

2422    def add_row(self, *cells: Any) -> Row:
2423        """Append one data row and return its ``Row`` object.
2424
2425        Examples:
2426            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2427            >>> row = table.add_row(1, 2)
2428            >>> row.cells[1].content
2429            2
2430        """
2431        if self._columns and len(cells) != len(self._columns):
2432            raise ValueError(
2433                f"Row has {len(cells)} cells but table has "
2434                f"{len(self._columns)} columns."
2435            )
2436        if not self._columns and cells:
2437            for _ in cells:
2438                self._append_column("")
2439        row = Row(self, len(self._rows), cells)
2440        row._height = self._default_row_height
2441        while len(row.cells) < len(self._columns):
2442            row.cells.append(Cell(""))
2443        if self.from_bottom_left:
2444            self._rows.insert(0, row)
2445        else:
2446            self._rows.append(row)
2447        for index, current_row in enumerate(self._rows):
2448            current_row.index = index
2449        self._invalidate_layout()
2450        return row

2452    def _ensure_grid_covers(
2453        self,
2454        min_grid_row: int,
2455        max_grid_row: int,
2456        max_grid_col: int,
2457    ) -> None:
2458        if min_grid_row < 0 or max_grid_col < 0:
2459            raise IndexError("grid row or column index out of range")
2460        while len(self._columns) <= max_grid_col:
2461            self._append_column("")
2462        _, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)
2463        while grid_row_count <= max_grid_row:
2464            self.add_row(*([""] * len(self._columns)))
2465            _, grid_row_count = _grid_dimensions(self)

2467    def populate(
2468        self,
2469        row: int,
2470        column: int,
2471        columns: int,
2472        items: Sequence[Any],
2473        from_bottom_left: bool = False,
2474    ) -> Self:
2475        """Fill a rectangle of body cells starting at ``(row, column)``.
2476
2477        All indices are 0-based. ``row`` and ``column`` are **data-row**
2478        indices (the header is not part of ``row``). :meth:`cell` counts the
2479        header as row ``0`` when a header is shown.
2480        Items are placed in row-major order with ``columns`` cells per row—the
2481        same layout as :func:`~simetri.helpers.utilities.get_cell_pos`. When
2482        ``from_bottom_left`` is False, filling continues at ``row + 1``,
2483        ``row + 2``, … in increasing data-row order. When True, it continues
2484        toward ``row - 1``, ``row - 2``, … instead.
2485
2486        Args:
2487            row: Starting data row index (0-based).
2488            column: Starting column index (0-based).
2489            columns: Number of columns in each filled row (band width, >= 1).
2490            items: Cell contents in fill order.
2491            from_bottom_left: If True, advance toward smaller data-row indices;
2492                if False, advance toward larger ones.
2493
2494        Returns:
2495            Self: This table.
2496
2497        Raises:
2498            ValueError: If ``columns`` is less than 1.
2499            IndexError: If a target row or column index is negative.
2500
2501        Examples:
2502            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2503            >>> table.populate(0, 0, 2, [1, 2, 3]) is table
2504            True
2505            >>> table.cell(1, 0).content
2506            1
2507            >>> table.cell(1, 1).content
2508            2
2509            >>> table.cell(2, 0).content
2510            3
2511            >>> table2 = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2512            >>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
2513            >>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
2514            >>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
2515            >>> _ = table2.populate(2, 0, 2, ["a", "b", "c"], from_bottom_left=True)
2516            >>> table2.cell(3, 0).content
2517            'a'
2518            >>> table2.cell(2, 0).content
2519            'c'
2520        """
2521        if columns < 1:
2522            raise ValueError("columns must be at least 1")
2523        if row < 0 or column < 0:
2524            raise IndexError("row or column index out of range")
2525        if not items:
2526            return self
2527
2528        item_count = len(items)
2529        local_rows = (item_count + columns - 1) // columns
2530        if from_bottom_left:
2531            min_data_row = row - (local_rows - 1)
2532            max_data_row = row
2533        else:
2534            min_data_row = row
2535            max_data_row = row + (local_rows - 1)
2536        if min_data_row < 0:
2537            raise IndexError("row index out of range")
2538        max_grid_col = column + columns - 1
2539        while len(self._columns) <= max_grid_col:
2540            self._append_column("")
2541        while len(self._rows) <= max_data_row:
2542            self.add_row(*([""] * len(self._columns)))
2543
2544        for index, item in enumerate(items):
2545            local_row = index // columns
2546            local_col = index % columns
2547            grid_col = column + local_col
2548            if from_bottom_left:
2549                data_row = row - local_row
2550            else:
2551                data_row = row + local_row
2552            grid_row = _grid_row_from_data_row(self, data_row)
2553            self._cell_at_grid(grid_row, grid_col).content = item
2554        return self
2555
2556    def _rich_style_from_cell(
2557        self,
2558        grid_row: int,
2559        col_index: int,
2560    ) -> RichStyle | None:
2561        fmt = _resolve_cell_format(self, grid_row, col_index)
2562        bg = _resolve_cell_background(self, grid_row, col_index)
2563        style_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
2564        if fmt.get("bold"):
2565            style_kwargs["bold"] = True
2566        if fmt.get("italic"):
2567            style_kwargs["italic"] = True
2568        if "font_color" in fmt:
2569            style_kwargs["color"] = _rich_color(fmt["font_color"])
2570        if bg.get("fill") and "fill_color" in bg:
2571            style_kwargs["bgcolor"] = _rich_color(bg["fill_color"])
2572        if not style_kwargs:
2573            return None
2574        return RichStyle(**style_kwargs)

2576    def build_rich_table(self) -> RichTable:
2577        """Build a Rich ``Table`` for notebook display.
2578
2579        Examples:
2580            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2581            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
2582            >>> table.build_rich_table()  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
2583            <rich.table.Table object at ...>
2584        """
2585        rich_table = RichTable(
2586            title=self.title or None,
2587            show_header=False,
2588            show_lines=self.show_lines,
2589            min_width=self.min_width,
2590            padding=self.padding,
2591        )
2592        column_count = len(self._columns)
2593        has_header = _has_header_row(self)
2594        for col_index, column in enumerate(self._columns):
2595            fmt = _resolve_cell_format(self, 0, col_index)
2596            justify = _align_to_rich_justify(fmt["align"])
2597            rich_table.add_column(column.header, justify=justify)
2598        if has_header:
2599            from rich.text import Text
2600
2601            header_cells = []
2602            for col_index in range(column_count):
2603                style = self._rich_style_from_cell(0, col_index)
2604                text = self._columns[col_index].header
2605                if style is not None:
2606                    header_cells.append(Text(text, style=style))
2607                else:
2608                    header_cells.append(text)
2609            rich_table.add_row(*header_cells)
2610        grid_header_rows = 1 if has_header else 0
2611        for row_index, row in enumerate(self._rows):
2612            grid_row = row_index + grid_header_rows
2613            rich_cells = []
2614            from rich.text import Text
2615
2616            for col_index in range(column_count):
2617                cell = row.cells[col_index]
2618                text = _cell_display_text(cell.content)
2619                style = self._rich_style_from_cell(grid_row, col_index)
2620                if style is not None:
2621                    rich_cells.append(Text(text, style=style))
2622                else:
2623                    rich_cells.append(text)
2624            rich_table.add_row(*rich_cells)
2625        return rich_table
2626
2627    def display(self) -> None:
2628        """Show this table in a Jupyter cell using Rich.
2629
2630        Examples:
2631            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2632            >>> table.display()  # doctest: +SKIP
2633        """
2634        console = Console(force_jupyter=True)
2635        console.print(self.build_rich_table())

2641    def drawable_cells(self) -> list[Any]:
2642        """Return drawable objects stored in cells (row-major).
2643
2644        Examples:
2645            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2646            >>> _ = table.add_row("text")
2647            >>> table.drawable_cells()
2648            []
2649        """
2650        drawables: list[Any] = []
2651        for row in self._rows:
2652            for cell in row.cells:
2653                content = cell.content
2654                if _is_drawable_content(content):
2655                    drawables.append(content)
2656        return drawables

Documentation table with Rich notebook and vector export.

Cell indexing: 0-based column indices 0, 1, … everywhere. Use grid rows for cells, range(), and cell() (row 0 is the header when a header is shown; the next row is 1). Use data rows for row() and populate() (row 0 is the first body row). See the module docstring for the full convention. Header strings in columns=["A", "B"] are display labels only — not column coordinates.

Examples:
>>> table = Table(
...     title="Parameters",
...     columns=["Name", "Value"],
...     size=(2, 2),
...     column_align=[Align.LEFT, Align.RIGHT],
... )
>>> table.cell(1, 0).content = "n_sides"
>>> table.cell(1, 1).content = 7
>>> table.cell(2, 0).content = "skip"
>>> table.cell(2, 1).content = 3
>>> table.build_rich_table()  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
<rich.table.Table object at ...>
Table( title: str = '', columns: Sequence[str] | None = None, *, size: tuple[int, int] | None = None, from_bottom_left: bool = False, pos: Sequence[float] = (0.0, 0.0), show_header: bool = True, show_lines: bool = True, column_align: Sequence[simetri.base.all_enums.Align | str] | None = None, column_width: float | None = None, min_width: int | None = None, padding: tuple[int, int] = (0, 1), font_size: float = 10.0, row_height: float | None = None)

1894        target_column_count = 0

1896            if len(size) != 2:
1897                raise ValueError("size must be a (rows, columns) tuple")
1898            row_count, target_column_count = size
1899            if (
1900                type(row_count) is not int
1901                or type(target_column_count) is not int
1902                or row_count < 0
1903                or target_column_count < 0
1904            ):
1905                raise ValueError(

1907                )
1908

1911            and columns is not None
1912            and len(columns) > target_column_count

1914            raise ValueError(
1915                "columns has more labels than the requested size columns"
1916            )
1917
1918        explicit_headers = list(columns) if columns is not None else []

1922
1923        if explicit_headers:

1926            aligns = (

1935                    else _TABLE_DEFAULT_COLUMN_ALIGN
1936                )
1937                column = self._append_column(header)
1938                column.set_format(align=align)
1939

1941            self.add_row(*([""] * len(self._columns)))

Create an empty table with optional column headers and size.

Arguments:
  • title: Table title for notebook and vector output.
  • columns: Optional column header labels.
  • size: Optional (rows, columns) body size to pre-create.
  • from_bottom_left: Whether row indexing starts at the bottom.
  • pos: Northwest table position.
  • show_header: Whether to show the header row.
  • show_lines: Whether to stroke grid lines.
  • column_align: Optional per-column alignment list.
  • column_width: Default width applied to created columns.
  • min_width: Minimum total table width after layout.
  • padding: Cell padding for vector layout and Rich preview.
  • font_size: Base font size.
  • row_height: Default height applied to created rows.
Raises:
  • ValueError: If size is not two non-negative integers, or if columns has more labels than size[1].
Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> table = sg.Table(size=(2, 3))
>>> len(table._rows), len(table._columns)
(2, 3)
>>> bottom = sg.Table(size=(2, 1), from_bottom_left=True)
>>> bottom.cell(0, 0).content = "south"
>>> bottom.cell(1, 0).content = "north"
>>> bottom.row(0).cells[0].content
'south'
>>> no_headers = sg.Table(size=(1, 1))
>>> len(no_headers.cells.cells)
1
>>> sized = sg.Table(columns=["A", "B"], size=(1, 3))
>>> sized.column_headers
['A', 'B', '']

Range over the full grid (header row included when present).

Index as table.cells[grid_row, col] — both axes 0-based grid indices. Row numbering follows the table origin. With explicit headers and show_header=True, the header is row 0 only when from_bottom_left is False; with from_bottom_left=True the header is the last grid row. For body-only row numbers use cell() or populate() instead.

Examples:
>>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
>>> _ = table.add_row("z")
>>> table.cells[0, 0].content
'A'
>>> table.cells[1, 0].content
'z'
>>> table.cell(1, 0).content
'z'

2058        """Return an inclusive rectangular region (0-based grid indices).
2059
2060        Same row/column convention as :attr:`cells`: grid row ``0`` is the
2061        first row at the current origin. The header is included only when
2062        explicit headers exist and ``show_header`` is True. Column indices start
2063        at ``0``.

2066            row_start: Top grid row of the range.

2082            self,

2084            col_start,
2085            picked_rows[-1],
2086            col_end,
2087            explicit_grid_rows=tuple(picked_rows),
2088        )

def reset(self) -> Self: 
2233    def reset(self) -> Self:
2234        """Empty all cells and clear table, row, column, and cell styling.
2235
2236        The table keeps its current row and column counts, title, position,
2237        and visibility settings. Header labels are cleared because header cells
2238        are part of the grid.
2239
2240        Examples:
2241            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2242            >>> table = sg.Table(columns=["A"], size=(1, 1))
2243            >>> table.cell(0, 0).content = "x"
2244            >>> _ = table.column(0).set_format(align=sg.Align.RIGHT)
2245            >>> table.rows.height = 24
2246            >>> table.reset() is table
2247            True
2248            >>> table.column_headers
2249            ['']
2250            >>> table.cell(0, 0).content
2251            ''
2252            >>> table.column(0)._format
2253            {}
2254            >>> table.row(0)._height is None
2255            True
2256        """
2257        self.font_size = _TABLE_DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE
2258        self._format = {}
2259        self._background = {}
2260        self._header_row_height = self._default_row_height
2261
2262        for column in self._columns:
2263            column._format = {}
2264            column._background = {}
2265            column._width = self._default_column_width
2266            column.header = ""
2267            column.header_cell._format = {}
2268            column.header_cell._background = {}
2269
2270        for row in self._rows:
2271            row._format = {}
2272            row._background = {}
2273            row._height = self._default_row_height
2274            for cell in row.cells:
2275                cell.content = ""
2276                cell._format = {}
2277                cell._background = {}
2278
2279        self._invalidate_layout()
2280        return self

>>> table.column(0)._format
{}
>>> table.row(0)._height is None
True

def add_row(self, *cells: Any) -> Row: 
2422    def add_row(self, *cells: Any) -> Row:
2423        """Append one data row and return its ``Row`` object.
2424
2425        Examples:
2426            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2427            >>> row = table.add_row(1, 2)
2428            >>> row.cells[1].content
2429            2
2430        """
2431        if self._columns and len(cells) != len(self._columns):
2432            raise ValueError(
2433                f"Row has {len(cells)} cells but table has "
2434                f"{len(self._columns)} columns."
2435            )
2436        if not self._columns and cells:
2437            for _ in cells:
2438                self._append_column("")
2439        row = Row(self, len(self._rows), cells)
2440        row._height = self._default_row_height
2441        while len(row.cells) < len(self._columns):
2442            row.cells.append(Cell(""))
2443        if self.from_bottom_left:
2444            self._rows.insert(0, row)
2445        else:
2446            self._rows.append(row)
2447        for index, current_row in enumerate(self._rows):
2448            current_row.index = index
2449        self._invalidate_layout()
2450        return row

2483        ``row + 2``, … in increasing data-row order. When True, it continues

2492                if False, advance toward larger ones.

2496
2497        Raises:
2498            ValueError: If ``columns`` is less than 1.
2499            IndexError: If a target row or column index is negative.
2500
2501        Examples:
2502            >>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2503            >>> table.populate(0, 0, 2, [1, 2, 3]) is table
2504            True
2505            >>> table.cell(1, 0).content
2506            1
2507            >>> table.cell(1, 1).content
2508            2
2509            >>> table.cell(2, 0).content
2510            3
2511            >>> table2 = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
2512            >>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
2513            >>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
2514            >>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
2515            >>> _ = table2.populate(2, 0, 2, ["a", "b", "c"], from_bottom_left=True)
2516            >>> table2.cell(3, 0).content
2517            'a'
2518            >>> table2.cell(2, 0).content
2519            'c'
2520        """
2521        if columns < 1:
2522            raise ValueError("columns must be at least 1")
2523        if row < 0 or column < 0:
2524            raise IndexError("row or column index out of range")
2525        if not items:
2526            return self
2527
2528        item_count = len(items)
2529        local_rows = (item_count + columns - 1) // columns
2530        if from_bottom_left:
2531            min_data_row = row - (local_rows - 1)
2532            max_data_row = row
2533        else:
2534            min_data_row = row
2535            max_data_row = row + (local_rows - 1)
2536        if min_data_row < 0:
2537            raise IndexError("row index out of range")
2538        max_grid_col = column + columns - 1
2539        while len(self._columns) <= max_grid_col:
2540            self._append_column("")
2541        while len(self._rows) <= max_data_row:
2542            self.add_row(*([""] * len(self._columns)))
2543
2544        for index, item in enumerate(items):
2545            local_row = index // columns
2546            local_col = index % columns
2547            grid_col = column + local_col
2548            if from_bottom_left:
2549                data_row = row - local_row
2550            else:
2551                data_row = row + local_row
2552            grid_row = _grid_row_from_data_row(self, data_row)
2553            self._cell_at_grid(grid_row, grid_col).content = item
2554        return self

Fill a rectangle of body cells starting at (row, column).

All indices are 0-based. row and column are data-row indices (the header is not part of row). cell() counts the header as row 0 when a header is shown. Items are placed in row-major order with columns cells per row—the same layout as ~simetri.helpers.utilities.get_cell_pos(). When from_bottom_left is False, filling continues at row + 1, row + 2, … in increasing data-row order. When True, it continues toward row - 1, row - 2, … instead.

Arguments:
  • row: Starting data row index (0-based).
  • column: Starting column index (0-based).
  • columns: Number of columns in each filled row (band width, >= 1).
  • items: Cell contents in fill order.
  • from_bottom_left: If True, advance toward smaller data-row indices; if False, advance toward larger ones.
Returns:

Self: This table.

Raises:
  • ValueError: If columns is less than 1.
  • IndexError: If a target row or column index is negative.
Examples:
>>> table = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
>>> table.populate(0, 0, 2, [1, 2, 3]) is table
True
>>> table.cell(1, 0).content
1
>>> table.cell(1, 1).content
2
>>> table.cell(2, 0).content
3
>>> table2 = Table(columns=["A", "B"])
>>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
>>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
>>> _ = table2.add_row("", "")
>>> _ = table2.populate(2, 0, 2, ["a", "b", "c"], from_bottom_left=True)
>>> table2.cell(3, 0).content
'a'
>>> table2.cell(2, 0).content
'c'
def build_rich_table(self) -> rich.table.Table: 
2576    def build_rich_table(self) -> RichTable:
2577        """Build a Rich ``Table`` for notebook display.
2578
2579        Examples:
2580            >>> table = Table(columns=["A"])
2581            >>> _ = table.add_row("x")
2582            >>> table.build_rich_table()  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
2583            <rich.table.Table object at ...>
2584        """
2585        rich_table = RichTable(
2586            title=self.title or None,
2587            show_header=False,
2588            show_lines=self.show_lines,
2589            min_width=self.min_width,
2590            padding=self.padding,
2591        )
2592        column_count = len(self._columns)
2593        has_header = _has_header_row(self)
2594        for col_index, column in enumerate(self._columns):
2595            fmt = _resolve_cell_format(self, 0, col_index)
2596            justify = _align_to_rich_justify(fmt["align"])
2597            rich_table.add_column(column.header, justify=justify)
2598        if has_header:
2599            from rich.text import Text
2600
2601            header_cells = []
2602            for col_index in range(column_count):
2603                style = self._rich_style_from_cell(0, col_index)
2604                text = self._columns[col_index].header
2605                if style is not None:
2606                    header_cells.append(Text(text, style=style))
2607                else:
2608                    header_cells.append(text)
2609            rich_table.add_row(*header_cells)
2610        grid_header_rows = 1 if has_header else 0
2611        for row_index, row in enumerate(self._rows):
2612            grid_row = row_index + grid_header_rows
2613            rich_cells = []
2614            from rich.text import Text
2615
2616            for col_index in range(column_count):
2617                cell = row.cells[col_index]
2618                text = _cell_display_text(cell.content)
2619                style = self._rich_style_from_cell(grid_row, col_index)
2620                if style is not None:
2621                    rich_cells.append(Text(text, style=style))
2622                else:
2623                    rich_cells.append(text)
2624            rich_table.add_row(*rich_cells)
2625        return rich_table
